claim: For RLHF-tuned LLMs (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude), verbalized confidence emitted as output tokens is typically better-calibrated than the model's own token-level conditional probabilities.
stance_target: verbalized confidence can carry meaningful calibration signal for chat models, contrary to the target paper's finding that verbal 1-5 confidence fails
scope_conditions: RLHF-tuned closed models (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude); TriviaQA, SciQ, TruthfulQA short-form QA benchmarks
quoted_support: For RLHF-LMs such as ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Claude, we find that verbalized confidences emitted as output tokens are typically better-calibrated than the model's conditional probabilities on the TriviaQA, SciQ, and TruthfulQA benchmarks, often reducing the expected calibration error by a relative 50%.

claim: Unsupervised pre-trained (non-RLHF) language models produce remarkably well-calibrated conditional token probabilities, but RLHF fine-tuning is believed to degrade this calibration.
stance_target: motivation for why verbalized confidence elicitation is needed for RLHF models specifically
scope_conditions: pretrained vs RLHF-tuned LLM comparison, prior literature synthesis
quoted_support: Recent studies have shown that unsupervised pre-training produces large language models (LMs) whose conditional probabilities are remarkably well-calibrated. However, ... RLHF-LMs produce conditional probabilities that are very poorly calibrated.

claim: This paper evaluates confidence elicitation purely via prompting strategies (no fine-tuning or distillation), establishing the prompting-only baseline that later distillation methods (ConfTuner, ORCE, Uncertainty Distillation) are benchmarked against.
quoted_support: we conduct a broad evaluation of methods for extracting confidence scores from RLHF-LMs.

claim: No code-generation benchmark was tested in this paper; all evaluation is on short-form factual QA.
stance_target: domain gap: verbalized confidence elicitation literature has not addressed code generation
quoted_support: on the TriviaQA, SciQ, and TruthfulQA benchmarks
